BiblicalUsage: hêrôwn means conception, pregnancy. It occurs 3 times in all, and the passages I have picked — Genesis, Ruth, and Hosea — show it in its plain sense. I read it as a word that does its work quietly, without dressing anything up.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hêrôwn matters because God opens and closes the womb, and every child is His gift. I hold that reading it plainly keeps me honest about what God actually said.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
